title: How to Reduce PDF File Size Before Sharing
description: Understand why PDFs get large and how to make a smaller copy while checking image quality, fonts, pages and document contents.
intro: A PDF can become large because it contains high-resolution images, embedded fonts, scanned pages or duplicated resources. Reducing its size is a trade-off: the goal is a smaller file that remains readable and complete for its intended use.

sections.heading: Find what is making the PDF large
paragraphs: Image-heavy documents often account for most of the bytes. Scans can also be large because each page is stored as a picture. Fonts, attachments and duplicated page resources may contribute too.
If only a few pages are responsible, consider exporting or splitting those pages separately rather than applying aggressive compression to the entire document.

sections.heading: Choose a compression level thoughtfully
paragraphs: Image downsampling and recompression can reduce size, but may soften small text in scans, diagrams and photographs. Start with a moderate setting and inspect representative pages at normal reading size and at higher zoom.

Keep an uncompressed original. For legal, archival, print or accessibility workflows, verify that the resulting quality and document structure meet the applicable requirements before replacing or distributing anything.

sections.heading: Check the output, not just the byte count
paragraphs: After compression, compare file size and check text clarity, page count, rotation, links, annotations, forms and any signatures or metadata you rely on. A smaller file is not automatically a better file.

The PDF Compressor creates a compressed copy with selectable quality levels. Keep the original and review the output before sharing. If the size is driven by images in other formats, the Image Compressor may be more appropriate before recreating the PDF.

faq.question: Will PDF compression make text blurry?
faq.answer: Text stored as text usually stays crisp, but scanned pages are images and can lose detail when downsampled or recompressed. Inspect scans and fine print carefully.

faq.question: Can compression remove PDF pages?
faq.answer: Compression should not be used as a page-removal operation. Check page count and use a page-organizing or splitting tool if you need to change pages.

faq.question: Does a smaller PDF always load faster?
faq.answer: A smaller file often takes less time to transfer, but viewing speed also depends on the PDF structure, device, reader and connection.

faq.question: Should I overwrite my original?
faq.answer: Keep the original until you have checked the compressed copy and confirmed it is suitable for the intended recipient or workflow.
